sources.label: Approved agreement and design
sources.summary: C1 requires a ≤16 KiB packet and ≤256 KiB per-Epic aggregate; AC1–AC9 define additive schemas, seed injection, status/CLI, agent-mediated backlog transfer, and target-path reauthorization.

sources.label: Advance Epics specification
sources.summary: Shell entries require title and success hint, support provenance, and remain lightweight/promotable.

sources.label: Backlog specification
sources.summary: Backlog rows are independently Zod-validated JSONL records and promotion appends lifecycle state.

sources.label: Current sizing implementation
sources.summary: Epic entries have no cardinality cap; existing aggregate guard covers Change documents only.

sources.label: Official Zod documentation
sources.summary: Zod supports bounded string schemas; aggregate object checks can be expressed through refinement.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Shared optional packet schemas plus additive projection and CLI surfaces are the simplest spec-compatible shape. C1 is not met because the design maps the per-Epic budget to a Change-document guard that cannot observe Epic-shell packets.

blockers.finding: DDC3 relies on AGGREGATE_HARD_CAP for the per-Epic packet budget, but that guard sums only Change state.documents while EpicSchema permits an unbounded entries array.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Add an Epic-store or shell-mutation-boundary UTF-8 JSON-byte aggregate check that sums retained shell context_packet payloads plus the candidate packet and rejects totals above 256 KiB before persistence.

source.label: Current implementation and approved design
source.summary: DDC3 names the Change artifact guard; the implementation shows that guard projects documents only and Epic entries have no maximum.

validation.notes: KD1/KD2 use bounded Zod fields plus serialized aggregate validation, consistent with Zod bounds/refinement. Optional packet fields preserve rq-epicEntries01 and independently validated JSONL rows under rq-backlogFormat01/rq-backlogLifecycle01. KD6 retains pure backlog promotion. C1 remains unenforced.

tradeoffs: A store-bound aggregate check adds a bounded sum during shell mutation.
Structural enforcement prevents oversized aggregate state when command conventions are bypassed.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep DDC3's Change artifact aggregate guard
alternatives_considered.rationale: It cannot observe or bound Epic-shell packets.

alternatives_considered.option: Rely on per-packet cap and implicit entry count
Store context only in title, success hint, or proposal
alternatives_considered.rationale: It loses durable structured context and violates the approved title/success_hint avoidance.

alternatives_considered.option: Shared optional packet plus explicit Epic aggregate guard
alternatives_considered.rationale: Additive schema with enforcement at the only boundary that observes the complete Epic packet aggregate.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Before design approval, add and test a per-Epic UTF-8 serialized packet aggregate guard at the Epic mutation boundary. Retain KD1/KD2/KD4–KD6 after that correction.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Fail design validation until C1 has a concrete, tested Epic aggregate guard; then proceed with the otherwise additive design.
follow_ups: Episode advisory recall was unavailable on the active tool surface.
After C1 remediation, verify target_path hints do not bypass normal target_confirmed and confirmationEvidence checks required by AC9.

documents.proposal:
## Problem

Two ways to record future work exist, neither fits long-horizon planning:
1. **Real ADV change** — spawns a live Temporal workflow immediately (project already carries 33 Running vs ~8 active). Workflow-per-future-item does not scale.
2. **Epic shell** — workflow-free, promotable, agent-visible, BUT carries only `title` + one `success_hint` string. No durable context.

Epic shells are the right workflow-free primitive; the gap is **durable context** on shells AND backlog items, **context-carrying promotion** (same + cross-project), and **visibility** of the future roadmap in ZLauncher.

## What Changes

Add a shared `FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` as an optional, backward-compatible field on both `EpicShellEntrySchema` and `BacklogItemSchema`. When a shell is promoted to a change, the packet is copied verbatim into a labelled seed section of the generated proposal/problem-statement. The status projection surfaces future work (shells + backlog) with packet summaries.

## User Outcomes

- A user (or agent) can capture durable context — background, references, constraints, avoidances, early design direction, cross-project target hints — when creating a backlog item or Epic shell, without spawning a workflow.
- On promotion, that context flows forward into the proposal verbatim — no re-derivation from scratch.
- Future work is visible in status output without requiring every item to be a live change or an Epic member.
- Backward compatible: existing backlog items and shells without a packet continue to work unchanged.

## Affected Capabilities

| Spec | Impact |
|---|---|
| `advance-epics` (v1.13.0, 33 reqs) | New optional `context_packet` field on shell entries; context-carrying shell promotion |
| `backlog` (v1.0.0, 8 reqs) | New optional `context_packet` field on backlog items |

## Affected Code

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `types/epics.ts` | Add `context_packet?: FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` to `EpicShellEntrySchema` |
| `types/backlog.ts` | Add `context_packet?: FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` to `BacklogItemSchema` |
| `types/future-work.ts` (new) | Define `FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` with bounded fields + 16 KiB serialized cap |
| `tools/backlog-shell.ts` | `adv_backlog_add` accepts optional `context_packet` input |
| `tools/epic.ts` | `adv_epic_add_shell` accepts optional `context_packet` input; `adv_epic_promote_shell` injects packet into generated proposal seed |
| `utils/context-packet-validation.ts` (new) | Serialize + validate packet ≤16 KiB; per-field bounds enforcement |

## Scope

### In Scope
- `FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` definition with bounded fields (background, references, constraints, avoidances, design_seed, cross_project_target)
- Backward-compatible optional `context_packet` field on `EpicShellEntrySchema` and `BacklogItemSchema`
- Context-carrying shell promotion: packet copied verbatim into proposal seed on `adv_epic_promote_shell`
- Promotion provenance: source shell id + timestamp preserved
- 16 KiB serialized packet cap with per-field bounds (D2)
- `adv_status` output surfaces future-work summary (shells with packet presence)

### Out of Scope
- Dependency graph + resume projection (`blocked_by`, cycle validation, `WorkNodeRef`) — owned by `addDependencyAwareResume`, **already landed on trunk**
- 33→8 zombie-workflow reconcile (backlog `bl-bEd2-Jbi`)
- Changing the Epic/change Temporal workflow model (seeds stay workflow-free)
- Live target-project MCP capability loading (`improveCrossProject`)
- ZLauncher rendering changes in `~/toolbox` (follows the projection landing; separate cross-repo change)
- Backlog→change packet copy via `adv_backlog_promote` (pure record operation; promoter passes packet to `adv_change_create` explicitly instead — see Discovery Finding DF1)

### Must Not
- Must NOT treat a stored `cross_project_target.target_path` as authorization — cross-project promotion requires normal `target_path` confirmation/revalidation
- Must NOT alter `title` or `success_hint` semantics — they stay OUTSIDE the packet
- Must NOT create a unified entity merging backlog JSONL, Epic-shell projection, and active Change
- Must NOT make Epic membership mandatory for backlog items or one-off changes
- Must NOT add mutation verbs beyond `context_packet` on existing add/promote tools

## Constraints

- **C1**: Packet serialized size ≤16 KiB; per-Epic aggregate packet budget ≤256 KiB (protects Temporal continueAsNew ~1.8 MB hard cap in `types/artifacts.ts`)
- **C2**: `addDependencyAwareResume` (Capability A) has **already landed on trunk** — `WorkNodeRefSchema`, `blocked_by` on shells, resume projection all present. This change builds additively on top of A's schema; clean seam unchanged (B owns packet content, A owns graph topology)
- **C3**: Backward-compatible additive field — `.optional()` with Zod; no migration needed for existing JSONL backlog or Epic projections
- **C4**: `replaceRecoveryToolSprawl` (HARD dependency) already archived 2026-07-15 — cleared

## Discovery Findings

### DF1 — Backlog promotion is a pure record operation (REVISED from original proposal)
`adv_backlog_promote` (backlog-shell.ts:175 + backlog-store.ts:338) ONLY appends `promoted_to` metadata to the JSONL. It does NOT create a change or generate proposal content. The change must already exist. Therefore, "context-carrying promotion" for backlog→change is architecturally different from shell→change:
- **Shell promotion** (`adv_epic_promote_shell`): generates proposal at epic.ts:1575 — clean injection point for packet copy ✅
- **Backlog promotion** (`adv_backlog_promote`): pure record — packet copy must happen at `adv_change_create` call site (the promoting agent reads the backlog item's packet and includes it in the proposal) OR through `adv_backlog_promote` gaining an optional proposal-seed capability

**Recommendation**: agent-mediated packet copy (promoter reads packet, passes to `adv_change_create`). Keeps `adv_backlog_promote` pure. The context is captured durably on the backlog item; the promoting command (e.g. `/adv-proposal` or `/adv-epic promote`) reads it and injects into proposal.

### DF2 — Status projection is in-memory, not file-based
No `adv-status.json` file exists in `plugin/src` or `bin/adv`. Status is served by the `adv_status` MCP tool (Temporal Visibility query → in-memory response). The ZLauncher in `~/toolbox` must consume ADV state through a different mechanism (possibly `bin/adv status --json`). Surfacing future-work in status output means extending the `adv_status` tool's response shape, not writing a file.

### DF3 — EpicShellEntrySchema extension pattern confirmed
`EpicShellEntrySchema` (types/epics.ts:293) already carries an additive optional field from addDependencyAwareResume: `blocked_by: z.array(WorkNodeRefSchema).default([])`. Adding `context_packet?: FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` follows the exact same pattern — backward-compatible, no migration.

### DF4 — Schema-registry impact: none
`FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` is embedded inside tool arg schemas (as part of `adv_backlog_add` and `adv_epic_add_shell` args). Zod generates the JSON Schema automatically via `z.toJSONSchema()` in schema-registry.ts. No separate registration needed — the packet schema becomes part of the tool arg schema naturally.

## Context

### Packet schema (D1)
```ts
FutureWorkContextPacketSchema = {
  background?: string,                 // why this work exists (≤4 KiB)
  references?: Array<{ label: string; locator: string }>,  // ≤12
  constraints?: string[],              // ≤12, ≤512 B each
  avoidances?: string[],               // ≤12, ≤512 B each
  design_seed?: string,                // early direction (≤6 KiB)
  cross_project_target?: { project_hint?: string; target_path?: string; repo_url?: string }
}
```

### One-off vs initiative model (D4)
| State | Decision rule |
|---|---|
| **Backlog** | Uncommitted, unready, or genuinely independent; context-bearing inbox |
| **Epic shell** | Future work committed to an initiative roadmap, not yet workflow-active |
| **Change** | Ready to become active now; may be one-off OR Epic-linked |

Crisp rule: use an Epic only when several items share an initiative-level outcome, sequencing, or navigation need. A one-off promotes backlog → change directly; NEVER create an Epic merely to classify a one-off.
documents.problemStatement: Planning long-running initiatives with many future follow-ups forces a bad tradeoff today. Creating real ADV changes for future work spawns a live Temporal workflow per change (the project already carries 33 Running workflows vs ~8 truly-active — ~25 zombies), but the workflow-free alternative (Epic shells) can only hold a title + a single success_hint string. Neither path lets you durably capture the context an agent needs to later rework, align, sequence, or promote that future work — including future work targeted at another project. Agents re-derive key context from scratch on every promotion, and future/roadmap work is not surfaced in the ZLauncher project picker.

documents.design:
# Design

## Architecture Overview

Additive schema extension: one new optional field (`context_packet`) on two existing Zod schemas (`EpicShellEntrySchema`, `BacklogItemSchema`), backed by a shared `FutureWorkContextPacketSchema` in a new `types/future-work.ts`. The packet rides existing storage paths (JSONL backlog, Temporal Epic projection) with no new infrastructure. Promotion injection is a string-append to the existing proposal-generation site. Status/CLI surfacing is an additive response field.

```
types/future-work.ts  ──→  FutureWorkContextPacketSchema (shared)
         │
         ├──→  types/epics.ts: EpicShellEntrySchema.context_packet?
         ├──→  types/backlog.ts: BacklogItemSchema.context_packet?
         │
utils/context-packet-validation.ts  ──→  parsePacket() + assertPacketSize() + assertEpicAggregate()
         │
tools/epic.ts:
  adv_epic_add_shell.args.context_packet?
  adv_epic_promote_shell: inject packet into proposal seed
         │
tools/backlog-shell.ts:
  adv_backlog_add.args.context_packet?
         │
tools/status.ts (or adv_status handler):
  response.future_work = { shells: [...], backlog: [...] }
         │
bin/adv roadmap: render future-work rows
```

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — Packet schema shape (types/future-work.ts)

```ts
const MAX_BG = 4096;        // 4 KiB
const MAX_DESIGN_SEED = 6144; // 6 KiB
const MAX_ITEM = 512;        // per constraint/avoidance string
const MAX_ARRAY = 12;        // references, constraints, avoidances
const MAX_PACKET = 16384;    // 16 KiB serialized total

export const FutureWorkContextPacketSchema = z.object({
  background: z.string().max(MAX_BG).optional(),
  references: z.array(z.object({
    label: z.string().min(1).max(200),
    locator: z.string().min(1).max(2048),
  })).max(MAX_ARRAY).optional(),
  constraints: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(MAX_ITEM)).max(MAX_ARRAY).optional(),
  avoidances: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(MAX_ITEM)).max(MAX_ARRAY).optional(),
  design_seed: z.string().max(MAX_DESIGN_SEED).optional(),
  cross_project_target: z.object({
    project_hint: z.string().max(200).optional(),
    target_path: z.string().max(1024).optional(),
    repo_url: z.string().max(2048).optional(),
  }).optional(),
});
```

On parent schemas: `context_packet: FutureWorkContextPacketSchema.optional()`.

Per-field bounds are Zod-enforced at parse. The 16 KiB total cap needs a separate serialized-size check (Zod validates individual fields, not the serialized aggregate).

### KD2 — Validation utility (utils/context-packet-validation.ts)

Three functions:
- `parsePacket(input: unknown): FutureWorkContextPacket` — wraps Zod parse; throws on bound violation
- `assertPacketSize(packet: FutureWorkContextPacket): void` — serializes to JSON, checks ≤16 KiB; throws `ContextPacketTooLargeError` with actual size
- `assertEpicAggregatePackets(entries: EpicEntry[]): void` — sums UTF-8 serialized sizes of all shell entries' `context_packet` fields; rejects if total >256 KiB (262144 bytes). Called at Epic mutation boundary (adv_epic_add_shell before store write).

Called at: tool input validation (parsePacket), backlog write (assertPacketSize), Epic signal (assertPacketSize + assertEpicAggregatePackets).

### KD3 — Proposal seed section format (adv_epic_promote_shell)

Current injection point: epic.ts:1575-1578. Extend the generated proposal string:

```ts
let proposal = `# ${shell.title}\n\n## Intent\n\n${shell.success_hint}\n\n## Scope\n\n- Promoted from Epic ${epic_id} shell ${entry_id}.\n`;

if (shell.context_packet) {
  const ts = new Date().toISOString();
  proposal += `\n## Context Seed\n\n**Source:** Epic ${epic_id} shell ${entry_id}, promoted ${ts}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.background) proposal += `### Background\n\n${shell.context_packet.background}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.references?.length) proposal += `### References\n\n${shell.context_packet.references.map(r => `- [${r.label}](${r.locator})`).join('\n')}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.constraints?.length) proposal += `### Constraints\n\n${shell.context_packet.constraints.map(c => `- ${c}`).join('\n')}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.avoidances?.length) proposal += `### Avoidances\n\n${shell.context_packet.avoidances.map(a => `- ${a}`).join('\n')}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.design_seed) proposal += `### Design Direction\n\n${shell.context_packet.design_seed}\n\n`;
  if (shell.context_packet.cross_project_target) proposal += `### Cross-Project Target\n\n\`\`\`json\n${JSON.stringify(shell.context_packet.cross_project_target, null, 2)}\n\`\`\`\n`;
}
```

Only non-empty sections render. Provenance (source shell + timestamp) is always present when packet exists.

### KD4 — Status future-work rows (adv_status response)

Add `future_work` key to the status response:

```ts
future_work?: {
  shells: Array<{
    epic_id: string;
    entry_id: string;
    title: string;
    has_context_packet: boolean;
  }>;
  backlog: Array<{
    id: string;
    title: string;
    has_context_packet: boolean;
  }>;
}
```

Populated by scanning active Epics for shell entries + reading active backlog items. Bounded by existing backlog tail_limit (default 1000 lines).

### KD5 — bin/adv roadmap rendering

`bin/adv roadmap` already reads Epics. Add:
- Shell entries show `[ctx]` marker when `has_context_packet`
- Backlog items listed in a `## Backlog` section with `[ctx]` marker

Rendering is text-only; packet content is not dumped (only presence indicator).

### KD6 — Backlog→change packet flow is agent-mediated (AC8)

`adv_backlog_promote` stays a pure record operation. The promoting command (e.g. `/adv-proposal` or `/adv-epic`) reads the backlog item via `adv_backlog_show`, extracts `context_packet`, and passes it to `adv_change_create` as part of the proposal content. No tool change to `adv_backlog_promote`.

This is documented as a workflow convention, not a tool-level enforcement. The promoting agent is responsible for reading and carrying the packet.

### KD7 — Per-Epic aggregate packet budget enforcement (validator-identified gap)

The existing `AGGREGATE_HARD_CAP` in `types/artifacts.ts` / `_artifact-size-validation.ts` measures Change document sizes only — it does NOT cover Epic entry packets. C1's ≤256 KiB per-Epic aggregate budget needs explicit enforcement.

`assertEpicAggregatePackets()` in `utils/context-packet-validation.ts`:
1. Called at `adv_epic_add_shell` before the store write
2. Loads the Epic's current entries
3. Sums `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(entry.context_packet ?? {}), 'utf8')` for all shell entries
4. Adds the incoming packet size
5. Rejects if total >262144 bytes (256 KiB) with `EpicAggregatePacketsExceededError`

This is a bounded computation: iterate active shell entries (typically <50 per Epic), sum serialized sizes. No network calls, <1ms for typical Epic sizes.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Schema layer**: `types/future-work.ts` (new) → extend `types/epics.ts` + `types/backlog.ts`
2. **Validation utility**: `utils/context-packet-validation.ts` (new) — parsePacket, assertPacketSize, assertEpicAggregatePackets
3. **Tool inputs**: `adv_epic_add_shell` + `adv_backlog_add` accept `context_packet`; adv_epic_add_shell calls assertEpicAggregatePackets before write
4. **Shell promotion**: inject packet into proposal at epic.ts:1575
5. **Status surfacing**: extend `adv_status` handler with `future_work` key
6. **CLI rendering**: extend `bin/adv` roadmap command
7. **Tests**: per-layer unit tests (schema parse, bounds, aggregate enforcement, promotion injection, status shape)
8. **Schema artifacts**: `pnpm run schemas:generate` if tool arg schemas changed (they will — new optional arg)

## LBP Analysis

This is the preferred long-term approach because:
- **Minimal blast radius**: one optional field per schema, no migration, no new infrastructure
- **Follows existing pattern**: identical to `blocked_by` additive field from addDependencyAwareResume (`.optional()` / `.default([])`)
- **Clean seam**: packet content (this change) is orthogonal to graph topology (addDependencyAwareResume). No coupling.
- **Bounded by design**: 16 KiB per-packet cap + 256 KiB per-Epic aggregate cap prevent unbounded growth on the Temporal continueAsNew seed path
- **Deferred complexity**: no unified entity, no new workflow model, no mandatory membership — each rejected alternative would have increased coupling and migration risk

## Affected Components

| Component | Change type |
|---|---|
| `types/future-work.ts` | New file — schema definition |
| `types/epics.ts` | Additive — one optional field on EpicShellEntrySchema |
| `types/backlog.ts` | Additive — one optional field on BacklogItemSchema |
| `types/index.ts` | Re-export FutureWorkContextPacketSchema |
| `utils/context-packet-validation.ts` | New file — validation utility (parse, size, aggregate) |
| `tools/epic.ts` | Add optional arg to adv_epic_add_shell; inject packet in promote_shell; call aggregate check |
| `tools/backlog-shell.ts` | Add optional arg to adv_backlog_add |
| `utils/backlog-store.ts` | Pass context_packet through to BacklogItemSchema on write |
| Status handler (adv_status) | Add future_work response key |
| `bin/adv` | Extend roadmap command with future-work rows |
| `plugin/schemas/*` | Regenerated via `pnpm run schemas:generate` |

## Design-Derived Criteria

- **DDC1**: Packet validation (Zod parse + serialized-size check + aggregate check) must complete in <1ms per item — no network calls, pure local computation
- **DDC2**: `future_work` section in adv_status must not add >5ms to response time — bounded by existing backlog tail_limit and Epic entry count
- **DDC3**: Per-Epic aggregate packet budget (≤256 KiB) is explicitly enforced via `assertEpicAggregatePackets()` at the Epic mutation boundary (KD7), NOT deferred to the Change-level aggregate guard which only measures Change documents

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| R1: JSONL backlog with many large packets slows reads | 16 KiB cap per packet; existing tail_limit (1000 lines) bounds read scope |
| R2: Packet copy inflates proposal artifact beyond Temporal limits | 16 KiB cap ensures proposal stays well under artifact size limits |
| R3: Agent-mediated backlog packet copy (AC8) is a convention, not tool-enforced | Documented in agreement; promoting commands will be updated to read+carry packet |
| R4: Status query scans all active Epics for shells | Existing Epic scan already happens in adv_status; future_work reuses the same read with a filter for shell kind |
| R5: Per-Epic aggregate budget enforcement adds latency to shell creation | Bounded computation: iterate shell entries (typically <50), sum serialized sizes. <1ms. |

## Validator Result

Validator (adv-researcher, attempt 1): **caution** (advisory-only, not gate-blocking).
- Finding: C1 per-Epic ≤256 KiB aggregate budget lacked enforcement — existing AGGREGATE_HARD_CAP measures Change documents only, not Epic entries
- Remediation: Added KD7 (`assertEpicAggregatePackets()`) to enforce the 256 KiB budget at Epic mutation boundary
- Spec-law compliance: clean — optional packet fields preserve advance-epics rq-epicEntries01 and backlog rq-backlogFormat01/rq-backlogLifecycle01
- No blockers; no alternatives overlooked

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout: skipped — narrow additive schema change with clear extension points. Zero alternative approaches viable (the packet shape was researcher-validated; the promotion injection site is the sole proposal-generation path). No leverage shortcuts or reusable components to discover.

## Outcome
ADV change seeds (Epic shells, backlog items) carry a durable, size-bounded **context packet** (structured background) injected into the generated proposal on promotion.

Capture background once; every proposal from that seed inherits it, bounded + validated. Reduces rework/drift. Future-work inventory surfaced in `adv_status` + `bin/adv roadmap`.
